chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, He marks in his heart a spot of light in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are illuminated by it, until he becomes more eager for what is in your hands (Al-Wilayah) than you are; and when He intends evil for a servant, He marks a black spot in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are darkened by it.
So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to make err, He makes his chest straitened and narrow as though he were ascending to the sky.
ai.seo_question: How does divine guidance manifest physically and spiritually in the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical mechanism of divine favor (Tawfiq) and misguidance (Tadlil) through the imagery of light and darkness imprinting upon the heart, a concept central to Shia gnosis (Irfan). It explicitly links this internal spiritual state to Quran 6:125, illustrating how God's will manifests as either an expanded, receptive chest for Islam or a constricted, struggling one for those destined for error. The narration underscores that true insight is a divine gift, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on God's sovereign choice in guiding the hearts of His servants.
